root.label: Character types and Unicode
root.note: A character type holds one code unit; what a reader sees as a character may span several.

children.label: Character types
children.note: Six types hold code units; only some have a portable encoding.

children.label: char, signed, unsigned
children.note: Three distinct types; the signedness of plain char is implementation-defined.

children.label: wchar_t
children.note: Size and encoding are implementation-defined, 16 bits on Windows and usually 32 elsewhere.

children.label: char8_t, char16_t, char32_t
children.note: Distinct types for UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 code units; char8_t arrived in C++20.

children.label: Literals and encodings
children.note: A prefix chooses the element type and the encoding of a literal.

children.label: Prefixes u8, u, U, L
children.note: u8 is UTF-8, u is UTF-16, U is UTF-32, and L uses the wide literal encoding.

children.label: Ordinary literal encoding
children.note: Chosen by the compiler, for example GCC's -fexec-charset, independent of the source file.

children.label: Source encoding, C++23
children.note: Implementations must support UTF-8 source files; the translation character set is Unicode.

children.label: Char literal: one unit
children.note: u'\U0001F600' is ill-formed in C++23 because the code point needs two UTF-16 units.

children.label: Escapes
children.note: Escapes name code points or raw code units without depending on the source encoding.

children.label: Universal character names
children.note: \u and \U name a code point and are encoded per the literal's encoding.

children.label: Named and delimited, C++23
children.note: \N{NAME}, \u{...}, \x{...} and \o{...} have no digit-count limit.

children.label: \x versus \u
children.note: \x writes a raw code unit value; \u names a code point.

children.label: The char8_t break
children.note: In C++20, u8 literals changed type and old code stopped compiling.

children.label: Pointer conversion
children.note: const char8_t* does not convert to const char*, so assigning a u8 literal to const char* fails.

children.label: Stream output
children.note: operator<< for char8_t and const char8_t* on narrow streams is deleted.

children.label: Migration
children.note: Use u8string, cast deliberately, or use an ordinary literal when it is UTF-8.

children.label: Library limits
children.note: The library counts code units and classifies single bytes; Unicode logic is yours.

children.label: cctype negative char
children.note: Arguments must fit unsigned char or equal EOF, so cast a plain char before calling.

children.label: Code units versus graphemes
children.note: size() counts code units; e plus a combining accent is three UTF-8 units but one grapheme.

children.label: format width
children.note: std::format estimates column width and truncates precision by whole grapheme clusters.

children.label: No normalization
children.note: The standard library has no normalization, collation or grapheme segmentation.

children.label: Conversion and detection
children.note: The old converters are on their way out; C++26 adds a way to identify encodings.

children.label: codecvt deprecated
children.note: Deprecated in C++17 and listed for removal in C++26; libstdc++ still ships it.

children.label: cuchar functions
children.note: mbrtoc8, mbrtoc16 and mbrtoc32 convert between the locale encoding and Unicode one code point at a time.

children.label: text_encoding (C++26)
children.note: Identifies an encoding by IANA name and id; literal() reports the ordinary literal encoding.
